evidence.docstring: Resolve a search scope to the directories it covers

problem: The hand-written scope list omits the `standalone` and `package:<path>` forms resolve_scope_paths accepts, and describes `all` as 'main + packages + namespaces' although it also covers the standalone directories. It doesn't say that a dotted `namespace:a.b` resolves under namespace `a`, which later examples (`namespace:company.models`) rely on.
replacement: Replace the bullet list (keep the 'Custom aliases' note as prose) with a fact block for `scopes.table`, as docs/api/README.md does.

problem: The numbered list restates the plugin-tool default order (scope_defaults.methods.<tool name>, then scope_defaults.global, then main) by hand.
replacement: Bind the order with a fact block for `scope.default.plugin` and keep only the why ('framework code usually lives in the main project') and the alias note in prose.

problem: The block calls internal JediAnalyzer methods on an undefined `analyzer`; find_models doesn't exist on JediAnalyzer at all (it is a Pydantic/Django plugin method), and find_symbol/find_subclasses are no longer MCP tools. A reader of this guide can only pass `scope` to the plugin tools.
replacement: Rewrite the block as plugin-tool calls a client can make: `find_pydantic_models(scope="main")`, `find_django_models(scope="all")`, `find_pydantic_models(scope="namespace:company")`.
subject: models = await analyzer.find_models(scope="namespace:company")

problem: find_subclasses was removed as an MCP tool in v2.0 (subclasses are now `expand(handle, edge="subclasses")`, which takes no scope), and `analyzer` is undefined. The example shows a call a client cannot make.
replacement: Show the list form with a plugin tool: `find_flask_routes(scope=["main", "namespace:plugins", "packages"])`.
subject: results = await analyzer.find_subclasses(

problem: find_routes is a FlaskPlugin method, not an analyzer method, and `analyzer` is undefined. The MCP tool is find_flask_routes.
subject: routes = await analyzer.find_routes(scope="backend")

problem: The scoped cache's TTL is PYEYE_CACHE_TTL (JediAnalyzer builds ScopedCache(ttl_seconds=settings.cache_ttl)), a configurable default, stated here as a fixed 5 minutes. The three-layer list also predates the file-artifact, Script and parso caches.
replacement: Replace the list with a link to docs/architecture/caching.md, which binds env.PYEYE_CACHE_TTL.default and describes the current layers.
subject: 5-minute TTL for analysis results

evidence.docstring: Load namespace paths only when needed.

problem: Says namespace packages are loaded on demand. The only lazy loader, LazyNamespaceLoader, is deprecated and used by nothing in pyeye; the example also calls the nonexistent `analyzer.find_models`.
replacement: Delete the Lazy Loading section (and its Table of Contents reach). A scope's paths come from the configuration each time a plugin tool searches; there is no separate on-demand namespace loading.
route_reason: This is an absence (no lazy loading exists), which neither a fact nor an executed example can show; the honest fix is deleting the section.

evidence.docstring: Find every project definition of *name* across the requested scope.

problem: Claims `analyzer.find_symbol("User", scope="all")` searches the namespace paths in parallel. find_symbol goes through _search_all_scopes, which looks the name up in the whole-project AST name index and filters by the scope's paths; parallel_search is used only for file globbing in JediAnalyzer.get_project_files. find_symbol is also not an MCP tool.
replacement: Delete the Parallel Search section: name lookups use a project-wide index filtered to the scope, so there is no per-path search for a user to tune.
route_reason: An internal search strategy isn't an exposed value an extractor reads, and no MCP tool call demonstrates it; the section should go.

problem: The user-facing way to see what a scope covered is the plugin tools' `envelope=true` option (it returns `searched` and `unsearched_scopes`). Instead the section recommends ScopeDebugger, a deprecated class built on the private `analyzer._resolve_scope_to_paths`, which only a pyeye developer could construct.
replacement: Call any plugin tool with `envelope=true` (e.g. `find_pydantic_models(scope="namespace:company", envelope=true)`) and read `searched` and `unsearched_scopes` to see which configured scopes the call covered; link docs/reference/tools.md for the parameter. Drop the ScopeDebugger block.
subject: Use the debug tools to understand scope resolution:

problem: Recommends the deprecated, unused ScopeValidator to users of the MCP server. An unknown `namespace:` scope is logged as 'Namespace not found' and an envelope call lists the configured scopes, which is what a user can actually check.
replacement: Replace the section with: an unknown `namespace:<name>` logs `Namespace not found: <name>`; call a plugin tool with `envelope=true` to see every configured scope in `searched` / `unsearched_scopes`.
subject: validator = ScopeValidator(namespace_paths, additional_paths, scope_aliases)

problem: There is no setting that enables parallel search, so this step refers to something a user can't do (and the version note is long past).
subject: Enable parallel search (automatic in v0.2+)

problem: .pyeye.json is read with json.load, so adding comments to it makes the file fail to load. Only the pyproject.toml form can carry comments.
replacement: **Document your configuration** - explain the namespace structure in comments in `[tool.pyeye]` (pyproject.toml) or in your README; `.pyeye.json` is plain JSON and can't hold comments
subject: Add comments explaining namespace structure

problem: The prose and the code comment restate trace's max_depth default (3) by hand ('max_depth defaults to 3', 'max_depth (default 3)').
replacement: Bind the default with a fact block for tool.trace.param.max_depth in the 'Bounded by two caps' bullet, and drop the number from the code comment ('raise max_depth or you will only see short cycles').

problem: The 'Bounded by two caps' bullet restates trace's max_nodes default (50) by hand.
replacement: Bind the default with a fact block for tool.trace.param.max_nodes instead of writing 50.
